title: Many Kinds of Bacteria Cause an Old Mushroom Disease
summary:
White button mushrooms are a popular food. But for more than 100 years, a disease called bacterial blotch has harmed them. It leaves brown or yellow spots, so the mushrooms are harder to sell. They may also spoil sooner.

For years, scientists mostly blamed one type of bacteria. Now scientists at the University of Florida have found that the disease is much more complicated.

The team collected sick mushrooms from several farms in the southern United States. They used DNA sequencing, which reads the genetic code of living things, and other lab tests.

They found more than 17 different kinds of harmful bacteria linked to the disease. Two well-known kinds were the most common. But the team also found a lot of another group of bacteria that had never been linked to the disease before.

Because so many bacteria may be involved, treatments aimed at just one kind may not work well. The scientists hope to find better ways to spot and stop the disease.
why_it_matters: Mushrooms are a food many families eat, so stopping this disease helps farmers grow more good mushrooms.
